original.reason: The proposed ordinal measure is never defined, its claimed behavior is unsupported, and the argument falsely treats Bob's existence of a winning strategy as excluding arbitrary infinite play. It also incorrectly infers finiteness of the state space.

judgment.reason: The claimed closure under every legal Bob move is false. From P being winning, a losing successor Q merely shows Bob should not choose P→Q; it does not contradict existence of some winning strategy from P. The final infinite-play contradiction repeats this strategy/existential-choice error.

Its closure fact is invalid: Bob's ability to force termination does not require every legal Bob move to preserve winning status. The conclusion that an arbitrary infinite play contradicts winning likewise confuses a chosen winning strategy with all Bob choices.

The switching lemma is false for the same reason: Bob may have a winning strategy at P without choosing the specified move to an unsafe Q. It also inconsistently calls the post-Bob position an Alice-turn position while using a Bob-turn safety definition. The final contradiction again treats safety as ruling out arbitrary Bob moves.

The asserted equivalence and closure are false: Q not being winning means Bob lacks a forcing strategy from Q, but this does not contradict P being winning when P has another winning Bob move. Thus the induction over arbitrary Bob moves and the final conclusion fail.
